official.deadline_note: The University of Porto's scholarships page publishes no application period. It states only that scholarships are grants intended for students enrolled in study cycles at U.Porto that fulfil the requirements, that students can benefit from more than one scholarship, and that scholarships are always awarded under the terms of the applicable law and of the Scholarship Regulations in force.
official.status_note: No current call or application window is published on the U.Porto scholarships page; the page is an overview that points to procedures, regulations and the Student Support Services rather than to an open call.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The page describes the awards as cash benefits; the only tuition-linked item is the Incentive Prize for first-year students, which the page states is equivalent to the value of the annual tuition fees for the respective study cycle. No page or period exists on which a scholarship student is automatically exempt from paying tuition.

verification.notes: The U.Porto scholarships page is an overview describing what scholarships are, the grounds for award (merit, economic and financial need), incentive awards and prizes for academic excellence, and directing applicants to procedures and regulations. It confirms a monthly cash payment contributing to course attendance costs and that students may hold more than one scholarship, but publishes no figures, dates or eligibility rules.

applicant_utility.summary: This page is an overview, not a call, and that is the single most useful thing to know before you plan around it: the actual rules, eligibility thresholds and application windows sit in U.Porto's How to Apply procedures and the Scholarship Regulations in force, and the page itself says awards are always granted under the terms of the applicable law and those regulations. Nothing here waives tuition automatically - the only tuition-linked item is the Incentive Prize for first-year students, which the page describes as equivalent to the annual tuition fees. Treat the monthly cash payment as a contribution to course attendance costs, not as a stipend that covers rent and living in Porto.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Already-enrolled U.Porto students with either strong grades (for incentive awards) or a documented economic and financial need, who can work through the university's own procedures and regulations.
application_readiness_checklist: Open the U.Porto 'How to Apply' section from the scholarships page and follow whatever procedures it specifies for your study cycle
Read the Scholarship Regulations in force rather than relying on the overview page, since the university states awards are granted under their terms
Contact the Student Support Services and your faculty's social action service early, since deadlines are not published on the scholarships page
Identify whether you are applying on merit, on economic and financial need, or both, because students may benefit from more than one scholarship
If you are in your first year, check the Incentive Award and Incentive Prize terms, including the rule that you must keep the corresponding grades in the two following years
common_rejection_risks: Relying on this overview page for deadlines and thresholds, which it does not publish
Assuming a scholarship means automatic tuition exemption - only the first-year Incentive Prize is described as equivalent to annual tuition fees
Missing the grade-maintenance condition attached to multi-year incentive awards
Failing to file the household and financial documentation that the needs-based route requires, because the overview does not list it
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition, unless you hold a specific first-year Incentive Prize, plus all living costs, transport and accommodation in Porto; the award is described only as a contribution to course attendance costs and U.Porto publishes no figure, so assume you fund the rest.
document_audit: The page publishes no document list, so the 'How to Apply' procedures and the Scholarship Regulations are the only reliable source
Means-tested applicants should expect to document household income and finances, since economic and financial need is a stated ground of award
Grade-maintenance evidence is needed for incentive awards carried into the two following years
alerts: Students may benefit from more than one scholarship, so do not assume one award closes the door to others
Awards are always granted under the terms of the applicable law and the Scholarship Regulations in force, which can change independently of this page
The page links directly to U.Porto's Student Support Services, which is where operational questions get answered
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Read the regulations and the How to Apply section from the U.Porto scholarships page, contact the Student Support Services for dates and requirements, then submit within whatever window applies to your study cycle.
